finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied `f` parameter is joined to the root without containment checks, so `../` sequences escape /srv/files and let an unauthenticated attacker read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (r.URL.Query().Get("f"), files.go:12)
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/dl", download) exposes the handler with no auth middleware
filepath.Join calls Clean, which resolves .. segments and yields /etc/passwd; the result is not checked to still be under root
file contents returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no strings.HasPrefix(cleaned, root+separator) check, no filepath.IsLocal, no allowlist, no authentication or authorization. filepath.Join only cleans the path and does not confine it. The /avatar handler is not affected because filepath.Base at files.go:22 strips directory components.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name), which only cleans the path, so `../../etc/passwd` becomes /etc/passwd. files.go:32 registers the handler with no auth, and files.go:18 writes the file contents to the response.
